findings.title: Team admin/owner check combines the two conditions with && instead of ||
findings.description: `isTeamAdminOrOwner` is computed as `(await isTeamAdmin(...)) && (await isTeamOwner(...))`. The name and intent call for "admin or owner", so this should be `||`. As written, a team admin who is not the owner (or the reverse) fails the check. The permission gate at the following `if (!isTeamAdminOrOwner && !isOrganizer && !isAttendee)` then rejects users who should be allowed to add guests.

findings.title: Blacklist lookup compares a lowercased list against non-lowercased guest input
findings.description: `blacklistedGuestEmails` is built with `.toLowerCase()`, but `guests` is filtered with `blacklistedGuestEmails.includes(guest)` without lowercasing `guest`. An input such as `Blocked@Example.com` bypasses a blacklist entry `blocked@example.com`.

findings.title: Email notification receives the raw `guests` input instead of the filtered `uniqueGuests`
findings.description: The handler computes `uniqueGuests` (dropping existing attendees and blacklisted emails) and creates attendees only for those. It then calls `sendAddGuestsEmails(evt, guests)`. `newGuests` is used in `sendAddGuestsEmails` to decide who gets the full scheduled invitation, so already-present or blacklisted addresses from the raw input can be treated as newly added guests.

findings.title: Email failure is swallowed with a generic log that drops the error
findings.description: The `catch (err)` block logs the fixed string `"Error sending AddGuestsEmails"` and never logs `err`, so the failure cause is lost. The handler then returns success even though notifications failed.

findings.title: Fallback toast message is unreachable
findings.description: In `onError`, `const message = \`${err.data?.code}: ${t(err.message)}\`` is always a non-empty string, so `message || t("unable_to_add_guests")` always evaluates to `message`. The fallback can never display.
